candidates.reason: FIFA is more authoritative, but openfootball remains more redistributable and easier to package as structured data. Keep FIFA as audit/import authority unless redistribution and structure are both solved.
Useful Football.TXT mirror, but not strictly better than the current CC0 CSV base on structure and long-history coverage for this package.
requiredGates: diff selected records before changing primary source

candidates.reason: Coverage can be useful, but license clarity and reproducibility are weaker than CC0 source-controlled CSV.
Current measured identity risk is already zero; Wikidata remains valuable for QIDs and aliases, not as a full replacement for registry/source-derived identities.
Wikidata can improve player aliases and QIDs, but should be filtered to roster/goalscorer players and reconciled rather than replacing the current Reep-derived provider ID subset.
Already selected as the roster authority; keep provisional/final status explicit.
Excellent open event data for covered competitions, but not a complete cross-league current-form source for every World Cup roster player.
Useful for clubs and market context, but redistribution rights and scraping fragility make it unsuitable as a package primary source.
Can improve live-ish match state with user keys, but quota, latency, and terms make it unsuitable as the offline historical data authority.
Useful fallback API, but user-key quota and coverage limits mean it supplements rather than replaces the static package.

layers.nextGate: Run FIFA fixture audit for group-stage and knockout schedule before publishing a new data release.
layers.reason: openfootball is structured and redistributable; FIFA is authoritative but better used as audit/import reference before redistribution.

layers.nextGate: Cross-check selected records against openfootball/internationals only if discrepancies appear.
layers.reason: Long-running CC0 CSV history remains the best free base for head-to-head, form, tournament, and shootout summaries.

layers.nextGate: Use Wikidata/FIFA IDs as enrichment, not as a blocker, unless identity-gaps.json regresses.
layers.reason: Registry protects the 48 World Cup teams and historical teams carry sourceRefs without duplicate FIFA-code risk; Wikidata remains an optional official-ID enrichment.

layers.nextGate: After official rosters are imported, filter Reep/Wikidata identities to roster and known-goalscorer players.
layers.reason: Reep is valuable for provider IDs, but only filtered player identities should ship in the plugin package.

layers.nextGate: Keep final roster input under release audit and update only from official FIFA or federation sources.
layers.reason: FIFA final squad lists are packaged as official roster facts with source URLs and rosterStatus=final.

layers.nextGate: Only publish cited derived summaries after license/legal review and official roster linkage.
layers.reason: Useful for analysis, but raw redistribution and cross-league completeness are weaker than Phase A sources.

layers.nextGate: Keep API quota, cache TTL, and provider fallback separate from the static data package.
layers.reason: Free quota APIs can supplement live-ish state with user keys, but they are not the offline historical data authority.

purpose: Machine-readable source decisions for package QA, extension UI, and agent routing.

rejectedAsPrimary.reason: Useful scraper framework, not a redistributable canonical data source for this package.
Useful extraction toolkit, but not strictly better than current CC0 raw sources for packaged facts.
Good qualitative context, not stable enough for canonical structured facts.

switchPolicy.reason: No single free public source is strictly better than the current Phase A combination for all required data layers.
switchPolicy.rule: Do not replace a current primary source unless the candidate is strictly better on authority, license, structure, coverage, and redistributability.
